22 A toy drone emits a sound of constant frequency 800 Hz. The speed of the sound in the air is
330 m s–1.
The drone moves along a straight path directly towards an observer and then continues in a
straight line directly away from the observer. The speed of the drone is constant.
toy drone
observer
What is the velocity of the drone when the frequency of the sound heard by the observer is
850 Hz?
magnitude of
velocity / m s–1
direction of velocity
A
19
away from the observer
B
21
away from the observer
C
19
towards the observer
D
21
towards the observer

hints: Notice the observed $850 \text{ Hz}$ is greater than the emitted $800 \text{ Hz}$ - recall whether approach or recession compresses the sound waves.
For a source moving towards a stationary observer use $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Rearrange to $v - v_s = v \times f_s/f_o$, calculate $330 \times 800/850$, then subtract from $330$ to find the drone speed in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Observed frequency $850 \text{ Hz}$ is higher than source frequency $800 \text{ Hz}$. For sound, a higher pitch means the waves are compressed, so the drone must be moving towards the observer.
Use the Doppler equation for an approaching source and stationary observer: $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$, where $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is wave speed and $v_s$ is source speed.
Substitute values: $850 = 800 \times 330/(330 - v_s)$. Rearrange to $330 - v_s = 330 \times 800/850$.
Calculate the effective wavelength term: $330 \times 800/850 \approx 310.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in speed units.
Hence $v_s = 330 - 310.6 \approx 19.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, about $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with sensible precision.
Magnitude about $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ directed towards the observer matches the table row. This is option C.

A.explanation: The speed $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is correct but moving away stretches the waves and would give an observed frequency below $800 \text{ Hz}$, not $850 \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Moving away from the observer cannot raise the observed $850 \text{ Hz}$ above the emitted $800 \text{ Hz}$, and $21 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ does not satisfy the Doppler equation.

C.explanation: Approaching shortens the observed wavelength so $850 \text{ Hz} > 800 \text{ Hz}$, and $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s)$ gives $v_s$ about $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the observer.

D.explanation: Towards the observer is the correct direction for an increased frequency, but $21 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is too large and does not satisfy $850 = 800 \times 330/(330-v_s)$.
